notation.meaning: Low-skill and high-skill labor (or any two inputs)
Wages, equal to marginal products under competition
Weight on $L$ in the weighted form used for the Cobb-Douglas limit

blocks.md: A CES production function describes how two inputs — say skilled and unskilled workers — combine to produce output, with a single dial that controls how easily one can stand in for the other. Turn the dial up and the two are near-perfect substitutes, like two brands of the same tool. Turn it down and they must be used together in fixed proportions, like drivers and trucks. Cobb-Douglas is the setting in the middle.

blocks.title: Why it matters
blocks.md: That one dial, the elasticity of substitution, decides how wages respond when one input becomes more plentiful — the heart of the skill-premium model.

- $\sigma > 0$ is the [Elasticity of Substitution](note:elasticity-of-substitution) between $L$ and $H$ — constant everywhere, hence the name.
- $A_L, A_H$ are [Factor-Augmenting Technology](note:factor-augmenting-technology) terms: $A_H H$ is skilled labour in efficiency units.

| $\sigma$ | Form | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| $\to\infty$ | $Y = A_L L + A_H H$ | Perfect substitutes |
| $= 1$ | [Cobb-Douglas Production Function](note:cobb-douglas-production-function) — the limit, by [L'Hôpital's Rule](note:lhopitals-rule), of the weighted form $[a(A_L L)^\rho + (1-a)(A_H H)^\rho]^{1/\rho}$ (without the weights the bracket above has no finite nonzero limit as $\rho \to 0$) | Factor shares constant |
| $\to 0$ | Leontief, $\min(A_L L, A_H H)$ | Perfect complements |
With output price $p$ and competitive labour markets, each factor earns its marginal product:

blocks.tex: w_L = p\frac{\partial Y}{\partial L} = pA_L^{\frac{\sigma-1}{\sigma}}\left(\frac{L}{Y}\right)^{-\frac{1}{\sigma}}, \qquad w_H = p\frac{\partial Y}{\partial H} = pA_H^{\frac{\sigma-1}{\sigma}}\left(\frac{H}{Y}\right)^{-\frac{1}{\sigma}}

blocks.md: Dividing, $p$ and $Y$ cancel — and because CES has constant returns, the ratio depends only on $H/L$ ([Homogeneous Functions and Euler's Theorem](note:homogeneous-functions-and-eulers-theorem)):
That log-linear relative wage equation is the core of the [Canonical Model of the Skill Premium](note:canonical-model-of-the-skill-premium).
